title: Something’s wrong with this meal

fn.en: Deal with a problem in a restaurant, and write the review the next day.

useful: Excuse me, there’s a problem with…

o: There seems to be a mistake.

items.s: Excuse me, could we have the ___, please? 🧾
The ___ was enormous — I couldn’t finish half of it. 🍽
The steak was ___ — grey all the way through. 🔥
You’ve ___ us for two coffees and we only had one. 💳
The food was ordinary, but the ___ was lovely. 🕯

lines: Excuse me, there [seems|seem|seeming] to be a mistake in the bill. ❌
I’m afraid this [isn’t|aren’t|not] what I ordered. 📋
Could you [possibly|possible|possibility] bring me a cloth? 💧
Don’t worry, it’s not your [fault|mistake|problem]. It happens all the time. 🤷
I’d like to [order|charge|apologise] something else, please. 🍽

sub.en: Look at the phrases. Which soften a complaint, and which soften an apology?

items.q: “Excuse me, there ___ to be a mistake in the bill.”
items.why: “There seems to be…” is softer than “There is…”. It leaves the other person room to check rather than defend.

items.q: “I’m ___ this isn’t what I ordered.”
“Could you ___ bring me a cloth?”
items.why: “Could you possibly…” is the most polite request form in the lesson.

items.q: “Would you ___ waiting a few minutes?”
items.why: Would you mind + -ing. And “yes” to this question means no.

items.q: The waiter apologises: “I ___ apologise.”
The customer says it doesn’t matter: “Don’t worry ___ it.”
“You’ve ___ us for two coffees and we only had one.”
“The vegetables ___ in the same water.”
items.why: RECYCLED from Lesson 29: the passive when who did it doesn’t matter.

use: There seems to be a mistake…
tts: Excuse me. I’m very sorry, but I’ve just spilt my orange juice. I’m afraid some has gone on the floor too. Could you possibly bring me a cloth? — Sure, that’s no problem.
I’m sorry about that. — Oh no, don’t worry. It’s not your fault. It happens all the time. Would you like another juice? — Oh yes, please. Thank you.
Excuse me? There seems to be a mistake in the bill. — Oh, is there? — You’ve charged us for two coffees, but we only had one. — I do apologise. I’ll get that changed for you.

acts.title: ★★★☆☆ Good food, one bad evening
text: We went on a Friday, four of us, without booking — which was our mistake, not theirs.

THE GOOD. The lamb stew is the reason to come. It is cooked slowly for about four hours and it is served in the pot it was cooked in, which keeps it hot to the last spoonful. The portions are enormous; two of us took a doggy bag home. The bread is baked there and it arrives warm.

THE PROBLEM. My steak came back undercooked twice. I sent it back once, politely, and the second time I gave up and ate the vegetables. The waiter apologised properly both times and it was taken off the bill without my asking, which is the correct answer to that situation.
THE ATMOSPHERE. Loud on a Friday — we shouted at each other for two hours. On a weekday I think it would be lovely: candles, wooden tables, a view of the street.
VALUE. About four thousand tenge a head with a drink. For the amount of food, that is good value.
The only downside was the noise and my steak. I would go back, on a Tuesday, and order the stew.

items.q: Why didn’t they have a booking?
o: they didn’t book — their own mistake

Would the writer go back?

write.q: Write a review of a restaurant you know: 8–10 lines. Follow the model’s six parts — when you went, the one dish worth coming for, the problem and what they did about it, the atmosphere, the price and value, and the one downside plus whether you would return. Use the passive at least twice.
write.model: ★★★★☆ Small, loud, worth it. We went on a Saturday evening, three of us, and we had booked, which turned out to matter. THE GOOD: the manty are the reason to come. They are made in the kitchen every morning and they are steamed to order, so you wait fifteen minutes and it is worth it. THE PROBLEM: the salad arrived twenty minutes after the main course. The waiter noticed before we said anything and it was taken off the bill. THE ATMOSPHERE: crowded and loud, with the kitchen open at the back, which I like and my mother does not. VALUE: about three thousand tenge each. Good value for the amount of food. The only downside was the wait for the salad. I would go back next week.

speak.q: Play both parts out loud: as the customer, raise two problems politely; as the waiter, apologise and offer a solution to each. Then say in three sentences whether you would go back.
speak.model: I’m afraid this isn’t what I ordered. — I do apologise, I’ll change it now. — There also seems to be a mistake in the bill. — I’m terribly sorry, let me check. — I would go back. The food was good and they fixed the problem without arguing. The only downside was the noise.
